items.title: Oil Monitor: Geopolitical Tensions Remain Despite Oil Selloff
items.summary: Oil and diesel prices have both eased, due to factors explored herein. But renewed tensions point to another potential round of escalation, and Middle East exports' sustainability is uncertain. In this note we offer detailed tracking of oil flows around the Middle East, Russia and China.

items.title: Uranium Outlook: Can Producers Fill the Supply Gap?
items.summary: We continue to expect uranium to trade above $100 a pound over the next three months, as nuclear energy demand is set to continue growing. Producer costs have kept rising, and we see limited appetite among them to meaningfully scale production. We offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: Walmart Reports Solid Third-Quarter Numbers
items.summary: Walmart reported solid third-quarter results and raised FY26 guidance modestly; we note four key positives from Buy-rated WMT's quarter. Looking to 2027, management remains confident despite transitory headwinds as new aspects of the business have higher profit margins.

items.title: EM Credit Weekly: The Macro Backdrop Still Warrants Caution
items.summary: We stay bearish on emerging-markets credit into year's end. Reaccelerating U.S. inflation and Fed tightening are keeping Treasury yields elevated, while a strong dollar adds to funding pressure and flows into the asset class. Favorable November-to-January seasonality is a risk to our call.

items.title: Australia's Labor Market Finally Starts to Loosen
items.summary: Australia's labor market loosened in October, with a clear underlying trend: There are ~80,000 fewer people employed since August, and the employment-to-population ratio is now below its early 2025 peak. We expect policymakers to hold rates steady until next year's third quarter.

items.title: We're Downgrading Transurban to Sell
items.summary: We're downgrading Transurban to Sell, with an A$13.90 target price. Soft October traffic growth indicates elevated fuel prices and cost-of-living pressures are hampering Australian road usage. TCL is trading in line with its historical ~4.5% dividend yield, likely leaving upside limited.

items.title: Correlation Corner: Between an Oil Shock and a Burst AI Bubble
items.summary: Cross-asset implied correlations are caught between pricing an oil supply shock and a burst AI bubble. For those looking to hedge equity downside, some of these dislocations from higher oil can provide good correlation entry levels for risk-off hedges. We highlight three opportunities.

items.title: Emerging Markets Credit Focus: 2027 Supply Outlook
items.summary: We forecast emerging-markets sovereign hard-currency gross issuance of $237 billion in 2027, down ~11% from 2026, with net supply remaining manageable. Sovereign technicals remain the more supportive of the two, while investment grade should continue to dominate corporate issuance.

items.title: U.S. Oil & Gas Exploration and Production: A Resilient Quarter
items.summary: Thie third-quarter E&P earnings season was characterized by strong operational execution and continued capital discipline, with companies largely topping production and cash-flow expectations, demonstrating resilience. In this note, we detail the key themes to emerge from the quarter.

items.title: Nvidia's Beat & Raise Drumbeat Continues
items.summary: Nvidia earnings reinforced our core investment thesis that demand remains very strong, supply constraints are easing, and interim management is confident enough to raise long-term growth expectations. We lift our 2026-28 EPS forecasts and offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: We're Raising Our Forecasts for South Korea's Growth
items.summary: We raise our South Korea real GDP growth forecasts for 2026 through 2028,  underpinned by a larger contribution from the IT manufacturing sector amid a prolonged memory upcycle. We keep our terminal rate assumption at 3.5%, expecting moderating core inflation and still-weak consumption.

items.title: Ignite Shows Further Confidence in Microsoft's Growth Drivers
items.summary: Microsoft's Ignite conference reinforced its efforts to broaden AI monetization beyond Copilot, with announcements and management commentary increasingly focused on enterprise knowledge, autonomous agents, security, and AI infrastructure. We offer further analysis herein.

items.title: Siemens Remains a Physical AI Winner
items.summary: Siemens' valuation gap to peers has substantially closed, due to its own outperformance as well as the de-rating of electrical/data-center and software peers. As Siemens remains a major potential beneficiary of the physical AI theme, we stay Buy-rated and increase our target price to €340.

items.title: We're Downgrading New York Times to Neutral
items.summary: While we remain confident in New York Times’s long-term outlook, we explore six near-term trends we see as eroding, ranging from falling app downloads to decelerating monetization. As such, we are lowering our target price to $76 and downgrading New York Times to Neutral.

items.title: Latin America Local Markets Scanner: November
items.summary: Despite sustained market volatility, a common theme across Latin America remains local rates' inability to keep pace with Fed-led tightening in financial conditions, as currencies broadly weaken amid eroding rate differentials.  We offer country-by-country analysis and thoughts on tactics.

items.title: Singapore Equity Strategy: Position for Defensives vs. Cyclicals
items.summary: We rate Singapore Underweight relative to ASEAN into next year's first half, setting an STI target of 5,325. Positive catalysts seem largely priced in; we recommend rotating away from crowded cyclicals toward value and defensives, and our preference is for large caps over small caps.

items.title: Previewing Key Themes for Our Basic Materials Conference
items.summary: Our 18th annual Basic Materials Conference will be held Dec. 1-2 in New York City. We will host fireside chats with EMN, AXTA, Air Liquide, WLK, FUL, DOW and PPG. In this conference preview, we highlight key themes, explore our latest market views, and update our rank order.

items.title: Citi China Conference 2026: The Paradoxes of Chinese Consumption
items.summary: We hosted Steven Barnett, former IMF Senior Resident Representative, at our 2026 China Conference. He sees China's low consumption share as reflecting an exceptionally high savings rate, not a low household income share, and identifies consumption as a rising policy priority.

items.title: Brazil Equity Strategy: Earnings Wrap-Up
items.summary: Brazil's earnings season proved constructive overall, with 40 of 72 Ibovespa names posting positive earnings surprises and 32 beating on revenue. Importantly, analyst sentiment deteriorated only marginally after the country's elections and sits near the top of its historical range.

items.title: Equity Markets Positioning Model: Conviction Remains Uneven
items.summary: Global positioning improved during the week, but the quality of flows differed materially across regions. In the U.S., much of the recovery was driven by short covering rather than new long flows, suggesting investor conviction remains limited. We offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: Inflation Weekly: Early Signs of Energy Pass-Through?
items.summary: Recent core inflation data have been stronger than we expected a few months ago. Some October details may offer the clearest signs yet that higher input and transportation costs are pushing up other prices, but given recent volatility, we need more data to judge the degree of pass-through.

items.title: Emerging Markets Economics: El Niño Monthly Tracker
items.summary: The Super El Niño is expected to peak in December, with conditions having varied effects across South America, from worsening flooding risk assessments in Argentina and Uruguay and the cancellation of Peru’s second anchovy fishing season to varying effects by latitude in Brazil.

items.title: Africa Economics & Strategy Weekly: Emerging Inflation Dynamics
items.summary: We look at which central banks across Africa could potentially be pushed into rate hikes during the coming six months, while also thinking about the outlook for the new government in Morocco following its September elections.

items.title: Introducing Our Emerging Markets Regime Model
items.summary: We introduce our EM regime model, a macro framework that classifies the fundamental backdrop for emerging markets via five stages: Recession, Stagflation, Goldilocks, Overheating, and Transition. We explain this framework further herein and offer key investment takeaways from our analysis.

items.title: Software Playbook: Positioning Into 2027
items.summary: Our Software Playbook outlines a more selective approach for 2027 as investors increasingly demand tangible AI adoption, monetization and estimate upside. We continue to favor infrastructure, data and security vendors with direct exposure to rising AI workloads, and highlight top picks.

items.title: North America Hardware & Storage: Third-Quarter Previews
items.summary: Hardware Enterprise Infrastructure OEMs should see strong results given a broader refresh cycle, bolstered by Citi’s third-quarter CIO survey and other factors. Concerns about peak AI demand, coupled with “over-earning” fears, have drastically compressed multiples and share prices.

items.title: Successful SpaceX Launch Adds Years to Its Moat
items.summary: SpaceX successfully conducted Starship Flight 15, a key milestone we’d flagged along a multiyear path of upside toward $900+, and we now have greater conviction in the outlook for the company’s Super Intelligence segment as well. We raise our target price to $280.

items.title: Key Takeaways From a Webinar With Construction Economists
items.summary: We offer key takeaways from a webinar with construction economists from leading industry organizations. Data-center and megaproject activity remain engines of the construction market; economists are a bit cautious given today's macro/policy backdrop but remain generally positive.

items.title: How Will Utilities Address Data-Center Concerns?
items.summary: The message from the EEI conference: Data-center growth will continue in states that can address public opposition via deals that protect utilities and consumers in downside scenarios. We look at states with the most-visible acceleration plans and ones in which creative ideas are emerging.

items.title: We're Downgrading Roblox to Neutral
items.summary: We remain bullish on Roblox’s long-term prospects, but in the near term we have concerns about four items explored within, from the waning popularity of Steal an Egg to concerns about fourth-quarter bookings. We're downgrading RBLX to Neutral, with our $55 target price unchanged.

items.title: European Media: Key Debates That Will Define 2027
items.summary: Following a resilient earnings season and a period in which AI positioning shifted favorably, we believe European Media enters 2027 in two-way debate territory. We outline key debates for each company in our coverage as we look ahead to 2027, and offer our preferred picks.

items.title: Citi China Conference 2026: Key Takeaways, Pt. 5
items.summary: We offer the fifth installment of key takeaways from our China Conference in Shanghai and Shenzhen, with links to our previous conference roundups. Names noted include Anta, Ecovacs, LONGi, Samsonite and XtalPi, as well as our takeaways about sectors and the macro environment.

items.title: Citi China Conference 2026: A Look at U.S.-China Stability
items.summary: We offer takeaways from a conversation with Tsinghua University's Wei Da at our 2026 China Conference. While cautious about 2027 and 2028, he argued that U.S.-China stability rests on structural forces including deep economic and supply-chain ties enabling “mutually assured disruption."

items.title: China Economics: Activity Weakens Across the Board
items.summary: China's activity indicators weakened across the board in October. We see building downside risks to our 4.6% year-over-year growth forecasts for both the fourth quarter and 2026. The global AI capex cycle could weigh on exports into 2027 and trigger more significant policy easing.

items.title: U.S. Rates Weekly: Staying Long 30y Break-Evens
items.summary: The latest inflation print and relatively hawkish Fedspeak remind us that front-end tail risks remain decidedly to the upside. Until inflation prints normalize, we stay neutral duration, but see being long 30y TIPS break-evens as the most attractive implicit short-duration trade right now.

items.title: U.S. Midterms: Implications for the Economy and Markets
items.summary: The  midterms shifted the balance of power in Washington, with Democrats winning majorities in both the House and Senate. We assess the implications of this tectonic shift for key areas shaping the economy and financial markets, including AI spending, fiscal policy and foreign policy.

items.title: U.S. Economics Weekly: Rate-Hike Debate Turns to Size
items.summary: Market expectations for Fed hikes took a sharp turn this week. We see 25-basis-point rate hikes in December and January as more likely than a 50-bp December hike, as Fed officials may still be cautious about recently tightening financial conditions, and offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: PULSE Monitor: Valuation Conundrum
items.summary: Nvidia’s 37% retrenchment has dragged the broader index down by 200 basis points; it would be wise to let this play out a bit longer. At the same time, our earnings review points to better positive surprise breadth, a possible signal of right-sizing of forward earnings trajectories.

items.title: U.S. Equity Strategy: Preparing for a New Normal
items.summary: Third-quarter earnings were solid but not exceptional, signaling a shift from recent quarters' extraordinary earnings tailwinds toward a "new normal." For 2027, we see fundamental puts and takes to both AI and non-AI-influenced parts of the market, as explored in this note.

items.title: PPI Details Are Less Suggestive of Energy Pass-Through Than CPI
items.summary: PPI final demand rose 0.3% month over month in October; core goods prices rose 0.55%, the strongest increase since May. But unlike CPI data, PPI details are less suggestive of persistently high energy and transportation costs pushing up other goods prices. We offer further analysis herein.

items.title: Global Macro Strategy: Writing on the Wall(er)
items.summary: Tuesday was a three-sigma day for hawkish Fed repricing judging by the 2y UST selloff. We explore why we see the door as now open to at least unwinding 2025's three insurance cuts. U.S. vs. G9 data momentum spread is widening; is U.S. exceptionalism back? Possibly, but it’s fragile.

items.title: The Anatomy of Market Peaks and Warning Signs
items.summary: AI-related weaknesses have revived comparisons with past bubble peaks. Leadership rotations have often emerged before broader market weakness becomes visible; in this note, we identify three warning signs that have historically appeared around major peaks, offering further analysis.

items.title: Nvidia Implications for Taiwan's AI Hardware Supply Chain
items.summary: Investors are asking if Taiwan's AI hardware ecosystem could suffer due to Jensen Huang's resignation and disruptions to Nvidia's roadmap. We think the primary supply-chain risk is a slowdown in platform upgrades, which could mean possible complications for the outlook from 2028 onward.

items.title: Oil Monitor: An Unsustainable Status Quo
items.summary: The latest U.S. "Gang of 8" discussions about Iran suggest near-term upside risks remain elevated. Absent a deal in the next week or two, we think Iran's incentives shift toward breaking and/or circumventing the “Iron Gate” blockade rather than waiting for a better negotiating environment.

items.title: Emerging Markets Strategy Weekly: A Mixed Environment
items.summary: We still worry a lot about supply/credit dynamics on the AI debt front and how that could drag on equity valuation in coming quarters. We still believe parts of the U.S. economy are feeling the pain from recent higher nominal rates: It's not a cliff, but a sign of a weak-ish patch.
